mechanisms.behavior: The drain feeds a four-ball trough. From drain to shooter, the known-working VPX script orders occupied switches 18, 19, 20, and 21; switch 22 is the stack/jam opto. Output 1 ejects the shooter-side ball and the script pulses switch 22 as the ball leaves.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough and up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 23 reports a ball in the shooter lane. Output 2 fires the automatic plunger to launch it.
mechanisms.label: Auto-launch assembly

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the Doc Ock hole closes switch 36. Output 4 ejects it toward the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Doc Ock vertical up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Output 3 enables the Doc Ock playfield magnet. The known-working VPX script binds the magnet directly to this modulated output.
mechanisms.label: Doc Ock magnet

mechanisms.behavior: Output 5 drives a relay for the 24 VAC synchronous motor and driver disc. Each activation advances the toy between its two limit positions; switches 57 and 58 report down and up, and target opto 63 is available in the exposed position.
mechanisms.label: Doc Ock motorized gate and target

mechanisms.behavior: A ball entering the Sandman hole closes switch 59. Output 12 ejects it toward the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Sandman vertical up-kicker

mechanisms.behavior: Output 13 drives a relay for the synchronous motor and driver disc. Each activation advances the assembly between down and up; switches 53 and 54 report those limits, and target opto 42 is exposed in the playable position.
mechanisms.label: Sandman motorized gate and target

mechanisms.behavior: Output 20 toggles the three-target bank between its lowered/playable and raised positions. Switches 9-11 are the individual target contacts; switches 49 and 50 report down and up. The known-working VPX script sets switch 50 when raising the bank and switch 49 when lowering it.
mechanisms.label: Sandman motorized 3-bank

mechanisms.behavior: Output 7 directly opens and closes the left control gate in the known-working VPX script.
mechanisms.label: Left magnetic control gate

mechanisms.behavior: Output 8 directly opens and closes the right control gate in the known-working VPX script.
mechanisms.label: Right magnetic control gate

mechanisms.behavior: Output 22 selects the loop-diverter route. In the known-working VPX script, energizing the output raises the diverter from its dropped default and de-energizing it drops the diverter.
mechanisms.label: Loop diverter

mechanisms.behavior: The left cabinet button is public switch 84 and the normally-closed EOS is public switch 83. ROM output 15 drives the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Lower-left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: The right cabinet button is public switch 82 and the normally-closed EOS is public switch 81. ROM output 16 drives the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Lower-right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: ROM output 14 drives the upper-right flipper. Dedicated upper-right button and EOS positions D15/D16 are explicitly unused on this machine.
mechanisms.label: Upper-right flipper

physical.notes: The physical VE manual installs and wires this Q19 coil. The known-working VPX leaves SolCallback(19) disabled, so its digital toy animation is intentionally incomplete evidence rather than proof that the physical output is unused.

physical.location: Sandman dome on the upper playfield assembly
physical.notes: The broad VPX FlashGiallo helper is outside the canonical table bounds; the physical LED is placed at the manual-defined Sandman dome assembly.

Two 113-5034-08 LED flashers are installed inside the single drilled Green Goblin toy. The normalized point locates that shared three-dimensional assembly; the manual does not expose separate playfield-plane coordinates, and the working VPX combines their light into one broad FlasherGoblin overlay.
SAM_FASTFLIPSOL synthetic state used for low-latency flipper gating; not a physical I/O Power Driver transistor.

physical.location: 32 playfield bulbs, 10 rear back-panel bulbs, and 2 coin-door bulbs on four fused GI circuits
physical.notes: The 32 playfield placements are measured from the circuit-colored bulb markers in the manual page-55 underside diagram, normalized in player view. The manual's circuit-4 prose says upper right, but its violet markers are on the upper left; the plotted physical markers are used because the brown/yellow marker regions independently validate the diagram orientation. The 10 individually measured rear-panel markers come from a separately captioned rear view, so x is mirrored into player view before projection to y=0. Two additional green/white-circuit bulbs are inside/on the coin door and intentionally have no playfield coordinate.
